analysis.title: Chinese trade continues to ride the global AI boom
key_insights: China's October exports grew 35.2% YoY, down slightly from 36.3% in September and a little below expectations (market 36.3%, ING 40.7%).
Year-to-date exports are up 22.7% YoY over the first ten months, at $3.78tn, which already exceeds last year's full-year total.
Auto export growth slowed to 37.6% YoY in October from 62.0% in September. The EU import quota on hybrid vehicles takes effect in December and could weigh on auto exports in coming months.
Household appliance exports slowed to 20.9% YoY from 31.7%, partly offsetting stronger tech export growth.
Tech exports accelerated in October: hi-tech 66.6% YoY, semiconductors 137.1%, automatic data processing machines 114.7%.
Export growth to ASEAN (46.3%), the EU (24.3%) and the US (32.9%) cooled slightly but stayed well above year-to-date rates. Exports to South Korea rose 92.4% YoY on strong tech shipments.
Import growth accelerated to 41.6% YoY in October from 31.0% in September, above market (33.9%) and ING (37.3%) forecasts. Year-to-date import growth is 29.0%, with total imports at $2.74tn.

High-tech imports rose 72.1% YoY in October (63.9% in September), bringing year-to-date growth to 50.8%. Semiconductor imports rose 78.3% from 74.7%. Imports of automatic data processing machines and parts rose 261.0%, slower than September's 296.5%.
Crude oil import volumes fell 13.3% YoY in October, but higher prices lifted oil import values 41.0%, the fastest pace since October 2022.

The October trade surplus fell to $104.5bn from $133.5bn, below market (125.8) and ING (131.2) expectations because of stronger imports. It is a 6-month low. ING still expects a record annual surplus in 2026.

Strong external demand has offset soft domestic consumption and investment in 2026. ING expects trade growth to moderate next year on base effects, while AI-related trade stays strong despite recent equity market volatility.

The US-China trade truce expires in January unless extended. Trump's visit to Shenzhen for the APEC summit next week is the next key window. Several European countries are debating new import quotas on chemicals, plastics and industrial machinery.

sector_views.rationale: China's tech exports and tech imports both grew strongly in October. ING expects AI-related trade to stay strong in the coming months.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong external demand and AI-related trade keep exports growing. The surplus is still on pace for a record annual high despite October's miss.
tension_points.bear_case: Stronger-than-expected imports pulled the October surplus to a 6-month low. Base effects may slow trade growth next year, and trade policy faces uncertainty from the expiring US truce and new European quotas.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The US-China trade truce expiring in January without an extension.
